newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: NATO plans key theme of Russia PM's Czech visit.
newsitem.headline: NATO plans key theme of Russia PM's Czech visit.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin begins a visit to the Czech Republic on Sunday with Moscow's opposition to NATO expansion high on the agenda for talks with Czech leaders.
The Czechs, along with Hungary and Poland, are leading contenders among former communist East European states to join the Western military alliance.

Moscow, which opposes the expansion, has demanded the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation should not station nuclear and other weapons in new member states and wants a binding treaty on relations between Russian and the alliance.
"We have already heard there is no plan to place (the weapons). We have already said clearly to everbody 'let's sign as you say'," Russia's ambassador to Prague Nikolai Ryabov told a news conference.
Chernomyrdin, the first Russian premier to visit the Czech Republic, is likely to press the issue in talks with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Monday.
"The Czech Republic is an independent sovereign state with its own foreign policy and certainly there must, and will be talks on this subject," Ryabov said.

The Czechs have said Russia's security concerns must be taken into account but say there can be no turning back on NATO expansion. "We will use this opportunity to talk with Russia about our position, our interest in becoming a full NATO member," said one Czech diplomat.

Reported remarks by Ryabov in March, when he hinted Russian economic deals with the Czechs could be jeopardised if they joined NATO, angered Prague. However, he told the news conference there could be no direct link between the Czech NATO membership and bilateral ties.

The Czechs have been totally dependent on Russia's Gazprom for natural gas supplies but last week officially signed a deal with Norway to import some 53 billion cubic metres of Norwegian gas over the next 20 years. Gazprom attacked the decision.

"We understand the Czech Republic's interest in the necessary diversification of gas supplies but I think we must draw the attention of the Czech side to the interests of its long-term, reliable supplier Gazprom," Ryabov said.

Relations between Czechs and Russians remain for many overshadowed by the 1968 Warsaw Pact intervention to crush the brief "Prague Spring" attempt to introduce "socialism with a human face" in then communist Czechoslovakia.
But a Czech Foreign Ministry spokesman said Yeltsin's description of the intervention as "inadmissible use of force" during a 1993 visit to Prague had helped heal official wounds.
"That was the Soviet Union, now it is Russia," the spokesman said.
